newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Q1 tourism down 17.3 pct on 1996 - statistics.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Q1 tourism down 17.3 pct on 1996 - statistics.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered a total of 458,629 tourists in the first quarter of 1997, down 17.3 percent from the same period last year, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Wednesday.

Of the total, Yugoslavs numbered 404,046, or 18.4 less than in January-March 1996. Visitors from other former Yugoslav republics -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- totalled 27,709, a 1.6 percent drop.

The number of foreign tourists dropped 14.1 percent from a year earlier. Most foreign visitors came from Italy (3,720), followed by Germany (2,249), Bulgaria (2,186), Greece (2,037) and Austria (1,742).
According to the National Bank of Yugoslavia, hard currency income from tourism in January-February 1997 totalled $4.5 million, down 8.2 percent from the same 1996 period.
Note -- Data is based on reception figures from hotels and other accomodation facilities. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
